liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Bird Song** (1 review): Sounds crisp and driving on the audience tape [19]
- **Black-Throated Wind** (1 review): Keith plays some nice transitional turns [22]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): Brilliant quiet section near the end suffers on the audience tape [24]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): Weir teases Truckin' at the end; the song finishes before they transition into it [22]
- **Truckin'** (1 review): Playin', Truckin' and The Other One all stretch out into long, hot jams [23]
- **The Other One** (1 review): Runs over 35 minutes; not a top version but quite good [13]
- **Stars & Stripes Forever** (1 review): Jerry, Bob and Keith linger after the encore, apparently waiting for Phil to return [23]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): Among the most impassioned versions of the period, with passion coming through on the audience recording [24]

## Setlist highlights

- **Other One Verse 1**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [25]
- **Other One Verse 2**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [25]

## The recordings

- **gd72-09-09.aud.pitch-corrected.zeb.31949.sbeok.flacf** (recommended): audience recording; 27 songs; 182 min; rated 3.83/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: Not as clear as the 4/29 tape, but better than other 1972 audience recordings; Clean-sounding low-generation tape, rare among traders in the old tape-trading days [1][20]
- **gd1972-09-09.149458.sbd.boswell.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: soundboard; 25 songs; 215 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd1972-09-09.aud.sirmick.32036.flac16**: audience recording; 24 songs; 197 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [9]. Said about its sound: Keyboards get lost in quiet passages on the audience tape; louder sections come through well [24]
- **gd72-09-09.aud.unknown.30991.sbeok.flacf**: audience recording; 25 songs; 193 min; rated 3.6/5 by 5 [10]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds great but is pitched down about a whole step, in the reviewer's belief; Very strong audience recording for 1972, though it runs slow and needs speed correction; Audience download runs at the wrong speed; reviewer made a speed-corrected version [10][14][15][18][19]

## Around the show

- Southern California crowd is heard whooping all over the room [20]
- Weir announces that Phil left through the back door with a woman [23]
- Reviewer ranks it below many stronger shows from the same period, though still solid [13]
- Crowd here is lively, unlike the oddly quiet German audience on 4/29 [20]
- Friend Of The Devil here differs from the versions at the Spectrum and Berkeley [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd72-09-09.aud.pitch-corrected.zeb.31949.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Zeb; source: Audience: Unknown Mics (pitch corrected) [1]. Also: Unedited apart from the tape flip in Truckin'; reel pauses left intact [1]
- **gd1972-09-09.149458.sbd.boswell.smith.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Debbie Stash and Will Boswell; transferred by Matt Smith, Scott Clusgston, Charlie Miller; source: Master Soundboard Cassettes (Uher deck) > Will Boswell's 1st generation reels @3.75 ips [2]. Also: A Sony ECM-22P source from Bruce Harvie and Rob Bertrando supplies crowd noise and the start of China Cat Sunflower [2]
- **gd1972-09-09.aud.sirmick.32036.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by SirMick; source: mac > cass (u/k gen) > wav > flac > wav > flac [9]. Also: Second source is a soundboard, copied mr > dat > cdr > shn > wav > flac; Soundboard patches fill brief spots in Playin' and Truckin'; distortion reduced and dropouts repaired [9]
- **gd72-09-09.aud.unknown.30991.sbeok.flacf**: source: Audience: Unknown Mics [10]. Also: Reviewer says it comes from the same source as their old tapes; Unedited except the tape flip in Truckin'; reel pauses left intact [10][15]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Hollywood Palladium - September 9, 1972](https://www.dead.net/show/september-9-1972) [26]
